catalog_quote: [p.71-72] Una is a language in which contrastive placement of pitch-accent carries a heavy functional load. The decision to consider Una a "pitch-accent language", instead of a word tone system with contrastive pitch on the accented syllable only, is due to the fact that each word has one and only one accent-carrying syllable which always carries a high pitch and has optionally more force. Monosyllabic words can be accented or unaccented. ... Polysyllabic words carry an accent on just one syllable which can be any syllable of the word. In Una the pitch of an unaccented syllable varies. But it is always lower than an emic high and it is about the same height as the following low. The following diagram shows the possibilities of syllables being accented on two, three and four syllable words, with examples of each pattern. ... audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: The tonal-OR-pitch accent coding rests on the dedicated primary phonology (Louwerse 1978, Irian 7(3):43-90), held as a page-image scan with scanned, and every deciding sentence was re-confirmed at pp.71-75 (author's explicit label 'pitch accent language'; one culminative high-pitch accent per word; placement contrastive and 'in most cases unpredictable'; two predictable subcases /-ɛb/ always accented, final [ə] never). The author's later reference grammar (PL B-100, 1988:9), also held, restates the same analysis and points back to 1978b. Glottolog 5.3 registers no other phonology or grammar for Una and no newer prosodic study was found, so the held source is the best available; the record's own note that lexical (free contrastive accent) would encode the same facts is accurate and is a labeling choice, not a sourcing gap.
